correctness.rationale: Normalize u by 2a+b=1 and use the positive Plucker relation r^2+t^2=s^2 on the stated symmetric x slice. Parameter r=s cos(theta), t=s sin(theta), theta∈(0,pi/2), and v=sin theta+cos theta∈(1,sqrt2]. The scale cancels and reduced log likelihood is g_b(v)=a log(v-1)+(a-1)log(v+1), giving exact derivative (1-bv)/(v^2-1). Sign analysis proves one symmetric strict maximum for b<=1/sqrt2 (quartic flat at equality) and two off-symmetric maxima for b>1/sqrt2; symmetric point then a strict local minimum. Solving (1+q)^2/(1+q^2)=1/b^2 gives the two exact reciprocal ratios. Independent SymPy verified derivative, exact quadratic roots, b=3/4 witness, and the quartic Taylor loss coefficient -1/(4 sqrt2). The argument makes no assertion about nonsymmetric full Grassmannian critical points.
